contentHtml:
New Delhi: The Drugs Consultative Committee (DCC) has recommended obtaining the opinion of the Directorate General of Health Services (DGHS) before taking a final decision on discontinuing the manufacture, import, and export of mercury-added topical antiseptics, including Mercurochrome/Merbromin.

The matter came up at the recent DCC meeting held on September 18, 2026, during deliberations on a proposal concerning the continued manufacture, import and export of mercury-added topical antiseptics (Mercurochrome/Merbromin) and approval for an extension of the exemption under the Minamata Convention on Mercury.

The convention seeks to protect human health and the environment from mercury emissions.

During the discussion, the committee was briefed on the status of mercury-added topical antiseptics under the convention. It was also informed that Mercurochrome in containers not exceeding 100 mL is included under Schedule K of the Drugs Rules, 1945.

The committee was further apprised that only a limited number of manufacturers appeared to be producing the product in the country, while alternative topical antiseptics were already available.

Considering these factors, the DCC observed that the issue should be examined primarily from the perspective of patient safety and clinical necessity.

DCC recommended that the opinion of the Directorate General of Health Services be obtained, along with the available data on manufacture and use of the product in the country.

A final view on discontinuing manufacture, import and export, as well as the consequential position under Schedule K, would be taken after considering the DGHS’s opinion.
